data.name: ProtocolSsdpDescription
data.value: SSDP (Simple Service Discovery Protocol) finds devices on the local network. The collector asks for Sonos devices using UDP multicast; players reply with their address. SSDP itself does not collect metrics.

data.name: ProtocolSsdpSetup
data.value: When and how do I use SSDP?

data.name: ProtocolSsdpWhen
data.value: Use it as additional discovery on a directly connected Sonos network. For routed networks or VLANs, the existing scan of allowed IPv4 networks is usually sufficient.

data.name: ProtocolSsdpInterfaces
data.value: Configure collection and allowed search networks. Enter the collector's own IPv4 interface address, one per line. Each address must exist in the API runtime; in Docker, the host IP is not automatically a container interface. Do not enter a speaker IP.

data.name: ProtocolSsdpNetwork
data.value: The selected interface needs multicast access to the Sonos segment. Allow outgoing UDP to 239.255.255.250:1900 and unicast replies to the ephemeral source port. This search uses TTL 1; ordinary routing, mDNS permissions or Docker port publishing do not provide that connection.

data.name: ProtocolSsdpLimits
data.value: Enable SSDP and save. The receive window limits waiting time (2–10 seconds); the datagram limit bounds replies per interface (1–256). Invalid replies also consume this limit.

data.name: ProtocolSsdpVerify
data.value: After the next full discovery sweep, check candidates, interface failures and limits on the Collection page. A candidate is admitted only after successful HTTP device identification on TCP 1400.

data.name: ProtocolSsdpFallback
data.value: The complete HTTP scan of all allowed networks continues. No SSDP reply does not mean a device is offline. SSDP does not expand allowed destination networks.

data.name: ProtocolGenaDescription
data.value: GENA (General Event Notification Architecture) delivers change notifications over HTTP. The collector subscribes to a device service; the speaker opens its own connection to the collector's callback address to send notifications.

data.name: ProtocolGenaSetup
data.value: When and how do I use GENA?

data.name: ProtocolGenaScope
data.value: Here, GENA accelerates group topology only: a ZoneGroupTopology hint triggers a current SOAP read. Volume, playback and network rates continue to use regular polling.

data.name: ProtocolGenaAddresses
data.value: Enable collection. The listen address selects the local listener interface; 0.0.0.0 binds all interfaces. Set the callback address to a LAN IPv4 reachable by speakers, usually the host IP in Docker. Neither 0.0.0.0, localhost/127.0.0.1 nor an unreachable internal container IP is suitable here. Enter an address, not a URL.

data.name: ProtocolGenaNetwork
data.value: Allow speakers to reach the collector's callback port (default 48081). In Docker, publish the same TCP port on the API container; the listening and advertised ports are identical. Routing and firewall must allow both directions: collector → Sonos TCP 1400, Sonos → callback address TCP callback port. Saving does not create firewall rules or publish ports.

data.name: ProtocolGenaTiming
data.value: Enable GENA and save. Lease duration is a request; the player grants the actual lifetime and the collector renews automatically. The initial timeout checks the first notification; the minimum interval limits extra event-triggered topology reads.

data.name: ProtocolGenaVerify
data.value: In device details, check both subscribed and initial notification received. A successful subscription alone does not prove the callback route. If the initial notification is missing, check callback address, port publishing and firewall. Players without the matching topology service are not subscribed.

data.name: ProtocolGenaFallback
data.value: Regular polling stays active when GENA fails. After a confirmed initial notification, an unchanged system may remain quiet for a long time; an old last notification alone does not prove a failure. GENA does not require SSDP.
